figures.question: How did 600 repositories become a useful evaluation collection?
figures.prompt:
Create a new publication-quality hand-drawn illustrated technical explainer for GitHub Manager. Use the attached local image as a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target and not a source of facts. Match its white paper, rounded dark pen outlines, legible handwritten lettering, blue and indigo headings, restrained purple accents and light blue/lavender marker washes. Use recognizable semantic objects (folders, source documents, magnifying glasses, human reviewer, friendly small robot). Favor a clear illustrated story over generic block diagrams. Landscape 16:9 composition, generous whitespace and margins, large readable text. Render every exact string and number accurately; include no invented metrics. Date/scope footnote: "GitHub Manager · recorded results · 19 October 2026". These are observed results, not future plans. TITLE verbatim: "From GitHub to a balanced repository collection".
COMPOSITION: A left-to-right illustrated collection journey across upper two thirds, plus a clearly separate human-review outcome along bottom.
LEFT: magnifying glass over GitHub repository documents; labels "Search by purpose, topic and project family" and "Read public evidence".
MIDDLE: two friendly curator robots examine README sheets through a sieve labelled "English-first + relevance checks". A retained-folder and a new-folder merge: exact labels "489 retained" and "111 replacements"; these merge into the final balanced collection, not into a second collection.
RIGHT/CENTER: display ten small recognizable folder stacks with these exact labels and counts, arranged as a tidy readable two-row shelf: "AI 60", "Cloud 60", "Commerce 60", "Data 60", "Developer tools 60", "Education 60", "Finance 60", "Healthcare 60", "Science 60", "Security 60". Shelf heading "600 public repositories · 10 areas × 60". All 10 folder labels must be present.
BOTTOM: a branching arrow from the collection goes to a PERSON with a clipboard, labelled "Selected human review: 30 repositories" and "83 confirmed label assignments". A second nearby paper note says "The other 570: processing checks only".
EXACT QUALIFIER prominently along bottom: "A balanced collection is not 600 human-approved answers."
No arrow that implies all 600 had independent double annotation. No scores or pass rates in this figure. Do not copy the style reference's old in-progress/future captions.

figures.question: At which stage did the system miss known labels?
figures.prompt:
Create a new publication-quality hand-drawn illustrated technical explainer for GitHub Manager. Use the attached local image as a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target and not a source of facts. Match its white paper, rounded dark pen outlines, legible handwritten lettering, blue and indigo headings, restrained purple accents and light blue/lavender marker washes. Use recognizable semantic objects (folders, source documents, magnifying glasses, human reviewer, friendly small robot). Favor a clear illustrated story over generic block diagrams. Landscape 16:9 composition, generous whitespace and margins, large readable text. Render every exact string and number accurately; include no invented metrics. Date/scope footnote: "GitHub Manager · recorded results · 19 October 2026". These are observed results, not future plans. TITLE verbatim: "Most missed labels never reached the model".
MAIN ILLUSTRATED JOURNEY: human answer-sheet clipboard on left marked "83 confirmed labels", magnifying glass sorting label cards in middle marked "69 found in the shortlist", friendly robot selecting cards on right marked "66 selected by the model". Arrows clearly mean processing of the SAME 83 known positive label targets, not repository counts.
BRANCHES: from the shortlist search draw 14 pale label cards aside, labelled "14 missed before generation". From the robot step draw 3 aside labelled "3 supplied but not selected". Label the 14-card branch with a small note "12 of these are Topics".
LARGE LEGIBLE SCORE NOTES UNDER JOURNEY: "Candidate recall: 69/83 = 83.1%" and "Final recall: 66/83 = 79.5%". A smaller note below the robot: "Of supplied positives: 66/69 = 95.7%".
SEPARATE SIDE NOTE (not mixed with misses): a small tray of new label cards marked "16 extra predictions: still unjudged". Do not mark them as errors.
EXACT QUALIFIER: "30 reviewed repositories · recall of confirmed labels, not overall accuracy".
This picture explains the measured bottleneck. Do not say 95.7% overall accuracy or show all candidate labels as correct. Keep the sparse search and robot mechanisms recognizable, with readable notes rather than a generic dashboard.

figures.question: Why can an output pass software checks while having incomplete recall and an unsupported claim?
figures.prompt:
Create a new publication-quality hand-drawn illustrated technical explainer for GitHub Manager. Use the attached local image as a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target and not a source of facts. Match its white paper, rounded dark pen outlines, legible handwritten lettering, blue and indigo headings, restrained purple accents and light blue/lavender marker washes. Use recognizable semantic objects (folders, source documents, magnifying glasses, human reviewer, friendly small robot). Favor a clear illustrated story over generic block diagrams. Landscape 16:9 composition, generous whitespace and margins, large readable text. Render every exact string and number accurately; include no invented metrics. Date/scope footnote: "GitHub Manager · recorded results · 19 October 2026". These are observed results, not future plans. TITLE verbatim: "Three checks, three different meanings".
COMPOSITION: three roomy illustrated comparison scenes left to right; friendly human answer-sheet, software clipboard/magnifying glass, and evidence-reading robot. Keep key numbers and definitions large enough for public sharing.
LEFT SCENE, heading "Recall": show two paper answer sheets with shared label cards highlighted; a human answer sheet marked "Known positive labels" and an AI sheet marked "Selected labels". Text: "66/83 confirmed labels recovered" then large "79.5%". Small question: "Did we recover the human's labels?"
CENTER SCENE, heading "Promptfoo": software magnifier checks real ID cards and numbered evidence pages. Large exact text "30/30 saved outputs passed". Beneath: "Valid category IDs + evidence references". Add exact caution "Not 100% semantic accuracy". Small question: "Does the saved answer follow the software rules?"
RIGHT SCENE, heading "Ragas grounding": a robot compares statements to highlighted evidence. Display three paper slips "Airbyte: 1/1", "Seldon Core: 4/4", "Python CDK: 3/4". Below exact text "Mean case score: 91.7%". Small question: "Does the supplied evidence support each claim?" A small magnified note shows "GraphQL support ≠ primary technology". Explicit small qualifier "3 cases · AI judge · no quality-pass threshold".
BOTTOM EXACT QUALIFIER: "Different questions. Different denominators. No exhaustive precision or F1 yet."
Do not invent a threshold or label all grounding results PASS. Distinguish existing evidence IDs from semantic support. White background, flowing illustrated objects and gently framed scenes, not three flat colored blocks.
